evidence.reference_title: KLICK Syndrome Linked to a POMP Mutation Has Features Suggestive of an Autoinflammatory Keratinization Disease.
evidence.snippet: Keratosis linearis with ichthyosis congenita and sclerosing keratoderma (KLICK) syndrome is a rare autosomal recessive skin disorder characterized by palmoplantar keratoderma, linear hyperkeratotic plaques, ichthyosiform scaling, circular constrictions around the fingers, and numerous papules distributed linearly in the arm folds and on the wrists.

nodes.description: KLICK epidermis shows patchy staining of the cornified layer with retained profilaggrin granules in the outermost cells. POMP-silenced tissue constructs show the same retention and altered profilaggrin cleavage products. The large keratohyaline granules seen by electron microscopy in the 1997 case fit this defect.

nodes.description: Proposed: chronic keratinocyte ER stress triggers innate-immune or type 1 interferon activation, which would make KLICK an autoinflammatory keratinization disease and explain the mild upper dermal infiltrate seen on biopsy. No inflammatory pathway has been measured in KLICK patients, and the PRAAS2 discovery paper describes KLICK as non-inflammatory. The observed infiltrate itself is recorded under histopathology.

evidence.reference_title: KLICK Syndrome Linked to a POMP Mutation Has Features Suggestive of an Autoinflammatory Keratinization Disease.
evidence.snippet: As we have cited that prolonged ER stress is known to induce inflammation in numerous chronic inflammatory skin diseases (23), the inflammation seen in KLICK syndrome could be considered to result from continuous abnormal ER stress in keratinocytes.

evidence.snippet: Although there are no reports of hyperactivation of innate immunity or of the induction of a type 1 interferon response in KLICK patients, the chronic ER stress present in the epidermis of KLICK patients may eventually trigger autoinflammation (16).

nodes.description: The outermost epidermal layers form abnormally, giving marked acanthosis, hypergranulosis and hyperkeratosis on biopsy. This is the shared tissue-level basis of the scaling, keratoderma and linear keratoses. Why lesions concentrate in palms, soles and flexures is not explained.

nodes.description: Patient epidermis shows altered POMP distribution. Silencing POMP in organotypic human epidermis by about half reproduced the patient staining pattern for POMP, proteasome subunits and filaggrin, supporting reduced POMP as the causal intermediate. POMP acts as a proteasome assembly chaperone by binding proteasome precursor subunits; GO has no molecular-function term for assembly-chaperone activity, so the binding activity is recorded with the general protein binding term, which is POMP's experimentally supported GO function.
